title: Annotatio V §.IV §.6: millennium heresy; baptism vs Supper necessity grades; analogy-of-faith charge abandoned
pass_a_gloss: But yet I myself granted at p. 80 in the Article on the Supper that heresy can be conceived in a wider sense; and whether that can happen is credible, asks A., if this Article in no way pertains to the foundation of faith. Resp. That the doctrine of the Millennial Kingdom of Apocalypse ch. 20 in no way pertains to the foundation of faith — whether it already obtained then, or is still to be awaited — the Author himself will have conceded; meanwhile how many heresies do the Wittenberg Lords even today elicit from what is still awaited? And from this very thing the most Famous Man will also understand how, by denying the Fundamentalitatem of the Article on the Supper while granting meantime that heresy broadly so called can be committed about the same article, I have contradicted my FAITH’S COMPANIONS — specially the Neostadians — the less, nay rather have wholly agreed with those who, not referring the Article on the Sacred Supper to the foundation of faith at all, yet confessed that certain things disputed about the Sacred Supper can touch the foundation of faith and incur heresy — especially since in nearly the same words (by which they hold the Contests on the Sacred Supper not to be mere word-fights and contentions about goat’s wool) I asserted the same. But when in the third place he strives to prove that I also contradict SACRED SCRIPTURE from this — that Scripture refers the teaching of baptisms, or the doctrine of Baptism, to the foundation (Heb. 6:2), and the Sacred Supper likewise with Baptism is a Sacrament — nay he cuts his own vineyards much more evidently than he will wish: those who hold the Sacred Supper likewise with Baptism for Sacraments, yet acknowledge their Necessity to salvation discriminated by many grades — so namely that they establish Baptism’s necessity as absolute, and thence are hardly persuaded of the salvation of unbaptized Infants even of Christians, or at least hesitate much about the same, while they admit even the Sacred Supper’s necessity only as ordained, whose deprivation does not damn, but only contempt. Fourth, while A. forces the contradiction designated by me, as it seems to him, against the whole Analogy of faith back at last to that Contradiction which fights with the Sacred Supper’s Nature and Character alone, with no new proof of this Contradiction added beyond those by which in his Anti-Irenic Tract he had fought for the Fundamentalitatem of the Article on the Sacred Supper, he forfeits his bail and falls with a great promised gap.
pass_b_english: Strimesius already granted (p. 80) heresy in a wide sense about the Supper. The millennium (Rev. 20) also fails the faith-foundation test, yet Wittenberg still wrings heresies from it. Denying Supper-fundamentality while allowing broad heresy matches his Neostadian companions.

Heb. 6:2 on baptism-as-foundation cuts the Author’s own vineyard: baptism’s necessity is treated as absolute, the Supper’s only as ordained (contempt damns, not mere deprivation). The analogy-of-faith charge collapses back into the Anti-Irenicum’s old proofs — bail forfeited.
source_text: At verò largitus tamen ipsemet sum pag. 80. in Articulo de Cœna: hæresin, latiori scil. sensu, concipi posse; id v. fieri posse num credibile est, quærit A. siquidem iste Articulus ad fundamentum fidei nullatenus pertinet. Resp. Ad fundamentum fidei nullatenus pertinere doctrinam de Regno Millenario Apocalyptico Cap. 20. Obtinueritne jam tum, an verò adhuc exspectandum sit? ipsemet Autor concesserit; intereà quot non numerô hæreses ex exspectato adhuc, eliciunt hodieque Domini Wittebergenses? Atque vel ex hoc ipsô intelliget quoque Vir Clariss. quomodo negando Fundamentalitatem Articuli de Cœna, largiendo interim, hæresin latè sic dictam circa eundem articulum committi posse, FIDEI MEÆ SOCIIS, in specie Neostadiensibus, contradixerim minùs, quin, Articulum de S. Cœna, ad fundamentum fidei haudquaquam referentibus, quædam interim de S. Cœna disputata fundamentum fidei attingere posse hæresímque incurrere fassis, ex asse adstipulatus fuerim, præsertim cùm iisdem propemodum verbis, (quibus illi Certamina de S. Cœna, non meras logomachias deque lana caprina contentiones esse perhibent,) idem asseruerim. Quando verò tertió locô, SCRIPTURÆ quoque S. me contradicere ex eo annititur probare, quòd Scriptura ten didachen baptísmon, vel, doctrinam de Baptismate, ad themelion, seu fundamentum referat. Hebr. 6, 2. S. Cœna v. perinde atque Baptismus Sacramentum sit; næ ille multò evidentiùs quàm volet, propria vineta cædit, S. Cœnam quidem perinde atque Baptismum, pro Sacramentis habentia, Necessitatem verò horum ad salutem multis gradibus discriminatam, agnoscentia, ita scil. ut Baptismi necessitatem absolutam statuant, indeque de non baptizatorum, utut Christianorum, Infantum salute, ægrè persuadeantur, saltem de eadem plurimùm hæsitent, S. Cœnæ etiam necessitatem, non nisi ordinatam admittant, cujus non privatio, sed solus contemptus, damnat. Quartò, dum A. contradictionem à me, ut ipsi videtur, adversus totam fidei Analogiam, designatam, ad eam Contradictionem postliminio coërcet, quæ cum solâ S. Cœnæ Natura & Indole, pugnat, nova nullâ hujus Contradictionis probatione adjectâ, præter eas, quibus in Anti-Irenico suo Tractatu, pro Fundamentalitate Articuli de S. Cœna decertaverat, vadimonium deficit & magno promisso cadit hiatu.
notes: Millennium; baptism vs Supper grades; analogy charge dies.
